articleTitle: Sketch-based Human Motion Retrieval via Shadow Guidance
abstract: Retrieving human motions is laborious and time-consuming because retrieving motions is not intuitive. In this work, we propose a sketch-based user interface for users to search the expected motions. First, we extract joint trajectories of skeletal motion data and construct a database. Second, the system searches for relevant motions in the database according to the query sketch results in real-time and generates shadow guidance that guides the freeform sketching of the trajectories. In addition, we performed a comparative study to evaluate the utility and effectiveness of the proposed user interface. It was verified that the proposed interface can capture users' retrieval intention which helps them retrieve motion data more intuitively.

articleTitle: Sketch-based Anime Hairstyle Editing with Generative Inpainting
abstract: In this work, we propose an interactive sketch-based design interface for anime hairstyle editing. The proposed system adopts the gated convolutional layer in the Generative Adversarial Networks model to achieve the generative editing of anime images. The generator network is based on an encoder-decoder framework with gated convolution to ensure the network can learn the random mask feature in image editing. The discriminator network uses the spectral-normalized architecture to preserve the stability of learning. In this study, we first collect and preprocess the dataset for data training. After that, we construct the user interface based on the pretrained model. Finally, we evaluate the system usage and user experience of the proposed editing interface.

articleTitle: Interactive Dynamic Projection Mapping onto Thin Plants with Bioluminescent Effect Animations
abstract: We propose a system to generate an interactive projection mapping onto thin plants automatically. Recently, projection mapping targets have included a wide variety of objects, ranging from buildings to fish. However, it is difficult to project onto dynamic and deformable targets such as thin plants. Our system tracks dynamic and deformable plants and registers the target projection area automatically. Our system also detects and recalculates vertices in the occlusion area for the interaction, e.g., a hand touching the plant. Therefore, our system can acquire the shape of occluded area. We also propose a system in which effect animations change interactively using occlusion detection with touch event detection via a capacitive sensor. In our system, four effect animations are applied to the targets.

articleTitle: Japanese Sign Language Recognition based on a Video accompanied by the Finger Images
abstract: Sign language is one of the most important tools for hearing impaired people to communicate with each other, and also a good tool to convey messages between hearing impaired and non-impaired people. Most non-impaired people, however, do not know the sign language, and there are many sign languages in the world, which are different depending on countries as with spoken languages. Then, many kinds of research have been performed in the world. Sign language is accompanied by the action using fingers, and the result of our previous work showed that the recognition rate of the words that have the same action with a different number of fingers was low. Therefore, we propose a sign language recognition method based on a video, which is accompanied by the finger images extracted from the overall image. As the result of the experiment using 3D CNN, the average rate of the recognition was 96.9%.

articleTitle: Sketch2Bento: Sketch-based Arrangement Guidance for Lunch Boxes
abstract: In recent years, sharing the images of the meals has been popular on social media as an artwork. In terms of the food culture in Japan, the lunch box is especially prevalent because of the lovely looking, such as character-bento. However, it is challenging and difficult to arrange a lunch box for common users without experiences and delicate skills. In this work, we propose Sketch2Bento, a sketch-based arrangement guidance system of food ingredients using spatial augmented reality technology. The proposed sketch interface allows users to design the blueprint of a desired lunch box. We then utilize the projection mapping to guide users with the projected arrangement hints in the boxes accordingly. Finally, we conduct a user study to verify the system usage and user experiences.

articleTitle: AR tooth brushing system to promote oral care habits of children
abstract: It is needed to be careful about the places where bacteria can accumulate while brushing teeth [1]. But it is difficult to teach young children to brush their teeth properly. By the way, the system about hand-washing for children that superimposes bacteria illustrations on the route of contact infection has been proposed in our laboratory [2]. In this study, we propose new AR system to promote oral care habits of children. It detects tooth areas easily soiled in real time using machine learning technique first, and superimposes bacteria illustrations to show easily soiled areas. It is expected that children learn good tooth brushing habit.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Effect of Art Content on Mental States Using Mirror Display with AR Function
abstract: As there are many opportunities to look in a mirror in daily life, an interesting theme is to investigate what kind of effect it has when art content is displayed together at that time. A mirror display that has a display function, as well as a mirror function, has been put into practical use. Using the AR function of the mirror display, we carried out psychological experiments in which art content is displayed along with one's face and full-body images and it was evaluated how it affects mental state. By preliminary experiments, ten video artworks that are considered appropriate were selected as art content. Next, 35 subjects were asked to read aloud the scenarios prepared in advance to induct the stressed state and the depressed state. Then they watched the mirror display where the art content is displayed together with their face and whole-body images. The difference in the mental state between the art-display and the non-art-display conditions was compared and evaluated. As a result, it was revealed that without art content there was not much change in mental state, but when art content was displayed, the depressed or stressed state was improved to a normal state.

articleTitle: The First-Person VR System Augmenting Folklore Experiences
abstract: Folklore is an essential cultural asset that reflects the lifestyle and thoughts of ordinary people who lived in those days and each region's cultural climate. However, a decline in the number of storytellers and changes in lifestyle have decreased the opportunity to come in contact with folklore. This article proposes the VR system in which users can experience a folklore story using voice and gesture from the first-person viewpoint as a main character of the story. This article aims to clarify what user experience can be provided through interactions with the world of a story and multimodal interactions with characters in the story by means of voice interaction and gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Virtual living room system based on video call to connect nursing home resident and family moderately
abstract: Many senior citizens stay in a hospital or nursing home. When they part with their family, there is a risk of them suffering from delirium due to stress [1] [2]. Although video call probably reduces their stress, they may feel an oppressive feeling by constant video call, and also may be hesitant to take the trouble to call each time. The family live freely and have no strong connection with the other in the living room, but a person can start a conversation at any time by talking to another person, and the conversation will end naturally without clear termination signal. In this paper, we propose virtual living room system to connect distant people each other moderately using video call service. It provides only information that the other person is there when video call is disconnected, and connects video call by a belief voice word.

articleTitle: Marine Biology VR Learning Support System Using Fish Swimming Simulation
abstract: It is important to learn biodiversity to create a sustainable society. In this article, we built “Marine Quest,” a VR learning system for studying marine creatures based on the swimming simulation of fishes. The swimming simulation was performed using the accurate fish simulation technology based on marine ecological and anatomical studies. Users can learn habitats, feeding habits, fish muscles, and swimming styles of various kinds of marine creatures as a diver exploring a VR Sagami Bay.

articleTitle: Visual Center Recognition in Game Concept Art Based on Art Principle
abstract: In the image analysis, the visual center is an area that has a high weighting factor for investigation. For instance, visual saliency is essential in image analysis. Furthermore, the visual center and visual guidance are necessary factors in composition when the 2D artist designs the concept art. Previous research is based on experiments or different saliency methods to identify visual interest rules. This research is inspired by bags of feature models and analyzes the frequency and color contrast in local regions to recognize the visual center. The authors intend to improve accuracy by using the bags of color model, and demonstrating the relationship between artists' pictorial skills and visual interest.

articleTitle: One-shot Line Extraction from Color Illustrations
abstract: Sketch colorization has been explored extensively using deep learning-based approaches. However, there are few works on the inverse problem of extracting lines from color illustrations, which is challenging due to the abstract illustration in cartoon rendering and the diversity of colorization style. In this paper, we propose a learning-based framework to explore one-shot line extraction from color illustrations. To avoid over-fitting, we simplified the proposed model and proposed a method for data augmentation when training using a single “color illustration-line drawing” pair. Then, we verified the model's effectiveness and efficiency in a group of color illustrations with similar colorization style. The experiments showed that the proposed, our method can outperform the conventional CNN (convolution neural network)-based sketch extraction methods.

articleTitle: A Motion Comic Creation with Monochromatic Background Extraction from a Comic Image
abstract: We propose a method for creating a motion comic with monochromatic background extraction from a comic image. The targets of the background are white, monochromatic screen tone, and solid black, and are extracted with an image processing. The extracted background can be applied to an animation such as translation, expansion, and dissolving. The background extraction method consists of a saliency map method, speech balloon extraction, and posterization with a pixel value of an input image. In our experimental evaluation with four comics, an accuracy of correction extraction is 49.2 %. The animation was manually generated with the background extraction, and a possibility for an attractive content is confirmed.

articleTitle: The Incidental Music Effector for Picture Books
abstract: In this study, we constructed a book shape multi-effector device for electric guitar to realize incidental ad-lib performance for reading around picture books. The multi-effector can be switched by the reader's page turning for the picture book. Also electric guitar acoustic effects and the acoustic effect sets are able to be created according to the story. In actual storytelling sessions using this multi-effector device, the electric guitar sounds changes accompaniment in accordance with the story. The incidental guitar improvisation, which is affected by the sound, also changes at the same time. This means that the reader intervenes with the incidental music. In order to realize this multi-effector device, we developed a switch mechanism that allows the user to switch effects by turning the pages of the book. In addition, we made it possible to set a loop for each page in order to accommodate a wide range of storylines.

articleTitle: A VR Experience of Being Warmly Swaddled Using Otonamaki and Haptics Device
abstract: To promote a positive understanding of pregnancy and childbirth, this study develops an experience-based content about fetus and pregnancy, which consists of “Into the Womb” and “Touch Love.” “Into the Womb” is a virtual reality (VR) system that brings users back into the fetal state using an artistic video and sound representation of the womb. “Touch Love” is a haptic transmission system that mimics the interactions between a mother and a fetus, such as a mother stroking her abdomen and a baby kicking. We conducted two experiments about the developed content. In the first experiment, we compared the heart rates of people whose entire body are swaddled by cloth using a Japanese technique called “Otonamaki” while experiencing “Into the Womb”, and those from the control group. The result shows no signs of mental stress caused by swaddling. The second experiment was conducted on people who had experienced pregnancy. We compared the impressions of the darker VR video of “Into the Womb” and those of the bright one. The results show no significant difference in terms of the brightness of the video. We also conducted evaluations of the fetal movement experience in “Touch Love.” All the participants answered that the haptics “resembled” the movement of the fetus in the mid-late stage of pregnancy. Throughout the experiment, the participants suggested that the developed content could give a good impression of pregnancy and childbirth.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Audio Dispersion Using Programmable Control
abstract: This paper presents a 6ch multi-channel non-ambisonic sound dispersion system utilizing of programmable control of sound location as well as other parameters. We have adapted this control system for a sound-art installation using national anthems generated by a variety of sources, with the choice of anthem, playback speed, spatial location and other parameters being under program control.

articleTitle: Designing an Experience Process for Digital Fabrication to Motivate Newcomers
abstract: The purpose of this study is to design the stages where newcomers in digital fabrication can learn. Although many newcomers are interested in digital fabrication, few of them can learn continuously. To overcome the problem, this study assumes that maintaining motivation will contribute to the solution and proposes a step-by -step experiential process that will enable the acquisition of basic skills without losing their motivation.

articleTitle: Procedural Rhetoric to Challenge Emotional Intelligence and Encourage Empathy and Compassion
abstract: Gathering a large team around emotionally challenging game projects is difficult, as there is no fixed vocabulary to share a strong vision of the game design of emotional intelligence-based games. This research connects research from psychology and game design theory, to establish principles and lexicon around emotional skills and mechanics.

articleTitle: Inheritance of Chinese Traditional Color Culture Based on Modern Human Visual Perception
abstract: With the development of the era and social changes, Chinese traditional color culture(CTCC) has gradually lost in the ancient books. To inherit the CTCC, it is necessary to satisfy the demands of the epoch and the aesthetic satisfaction of modern people. In this study, we propose a new approach that could inherit and develop CTCC. Through literature review, the historical background of the CTCC is defined and the necessity of research is interpretation, the connotation of the CTCC is elaborated, and the artwork form of Chinese traditional color is clarified. Based on the visual perception experiment, we obtained the modern Chinese visual perception, behavior data of the Chinese traditional color scheme (CTCS) as an input baseline to seek a general visual perception rule which could suitable for the aesthetics of modern people. This study proposes a systematic process of CTCS to seek an approach to inherit and develop CTCC.

articleTitle: Scenario-Based Customer Service VR Training System Using Second Language
abstract: Since a training system using VR can reproduce an actual training environment, training systems have been studied in commercial fields such as medical care and construction. This immersive experience in a virtual space can have a great effect on learning a second language. In this paper, we propose an immersive learning system that learns phrases used in the customer service industry in the customer service experience. We asked the subjects to experience the system, measured the effects of learning, and evaluated the system. Evaluating the learning effect of phrases used in customer service English on 8 students, all student achieved good learning results. Besides, to evaluate the usability of the system, the VR system was evaluated by performing SSQ to measure VR sickness shows this system doesn't cause virtual sickness, SUS to measure usability shows this system evaluation is higher than average system, and IPQ to measure presence in an immersive space shows this system gives average virtual reality experience.

articleTitle: Multimodal Interactive Game Interface to Increase Intimacy with Characters
abstract: Although the number of games using voice recognition has increased in recent years, psychological effects such as intimacy with characters on the screen when using voice dialogue have not been clarified. In this paper, we realized a game interface that uses voice dialogue in combination with controller operation used in conventional games, and compared it with conventional games in terms of the effect on intimacy with characters and the overall enjoyment of the game.

articleTitle: Visualization of Relationship between Facial Features and Impression Evaluations
abstract: Impression of facial images strongly relates to the tones and shapes of the faces. This paper presents our study on the visualization of relationships between facial features and impression evaluations. Specifically, we generate clusters of faces and then visualize the relationships between the clusters and impression evaluation results. This study applies a set of artificial facial images generated with a machine learning model and then extracts facial regions. We apply a clustering algorithm with features of the faces calculated based on pixel values and aspect ratios of the faces. Meanwhile, we conduct impression evaluations based on the SD method on the five-point Likert scale. This study integrates the clustering and impression evaluation results and visualizes the dataset by using our own hierarchical data visualization technique.

articleTitle: Stroke Correspondence by Labeling Closed Areas
abstract: Constructing stroke correspondences between keyframes is one of the most important processes in the production pipeline of hand-drawn inbetweening frames. This process requires time-consuming manual work imposing a tremendous burden on the animators. We propose a method to estimate stroke correspondences between raster character images (keyframes) without vectorization processes. First, the proposed system separates the closed areas in each keyframe and estimates the correspondences between closed areas by using the characteristics of shape, depth, and closed area connection. Second, the proposed system estimates stroke correspondences from the estimated closed area correspondences. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by performing a user study and comparing the proposed system with conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Interactive Dance Support System Using Spatial Augmented Reality
abstract: In this study, we propose an interactive dance training support system to promote an individual's motivation for practicing dance. In order to motivate the user, we designe a scenario of dancing with friends (virtual characters) by adopting a projection-mapping technique to create a large-scale augmented reality space. We project the dancing scene on a three-sided wall-type transparent screen to improve the sense of immersion. The proposed system assigns scores by comparison of the user's movement to a target dance movement in real-time. The reactions of the projected characters provide feedback to the user interactively according to the calculated score. The advisor character can verbally encourage the user when the scores are low. Finally, we conduct a user study to verify the usefulness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Application of Gamification to Online Survey Forms: Development of Digital Template System “Bingo Survey” and Evaluation
abstract: Nowadays, online surveys are commonly used in business and academic contexts with the widespread use of digital devices. However, problems around online surveys, such as reliability issues and frequent withdrawals of respondents have also been reported. Previous studies suggest that gamification is one of the effective solutions to these problems, and it was reported that gamified online surveys were beneficial in increasing respondents' motivation, response rates, and quality of responses. Despite the benefits, previous studies also pointed out that making a gamified survey took a lot of effort, and in some cases, game elements lowered the quality of responses. This study aims to develop a template system for gamified online survey forms and approach these problems. We applied an interactive digital Bingo game to online survey forms, with some other gamification elements such as instant feedback, score, and ranking. The system “Bingo Survey” was a digital template system for making a gamified online survey form. It was developed with TypeScript, React, and AWS Amplify. An experiment was performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the suggested system. 62 participants participated in the experiment. Each participant accessed online questionnaire form. Several conditions were set to compare forms made through our template system and traditional online survey forms. Participants, randomly divided into the conditions, answered experimental online questionnaires, and evaluated the effectiveness of the online survey form. As a result, the forms made with the suggested system were highly evaluated than the traditional online survey forms, for their enjoyability, effects for increasing motivation, and higher response rates for optional free comment sections. Furthermore, it was noticed that there were no significant differences regarding the quality of response values in the experimental questionnaires between the conditions.

articleTitle: Skeleton-Based Interactive Fabrication for Large-Scale Newspaper Sculpture
abstract: In this work, we propose a large-scale fabrication technique that uses newspapers with accessible and tractable properties. The system utilizes an interactive guidance system allowing common users to achieve large-scale newspaper sculptures from target 3D models. To maintain the fabrication shape, the proposed system provides an automatic design approach to create skeleton structures, which are formed from multiple chopsticks using the specialized connectors with 3D printing. Our system can support users in building complex newspaper sculptures. The interactive projection guidance is provided to visualize the differences between the depth maps of the target model and the current work so that the users can overlap the newspapers where needed. We evaluate the usefulness of the guidance system for fabrication support and the fabrication process with the proposed skeleton structure in our user study.

articleTitle: Reimagining Japanese Zen Garden with wave simulation
abstract: ‘Reimagining Japanese Zen Garden with Wave simulation’ is an interdisciplinary research project that explores the art of Japanese garden making and its modernity demonstrated through the researcher's evolving practice of art-science as a contemporary artist. A garden is a unique place where nature and humans meet. Instead of being the conflict, it seeks the harmonious amalgam of co-existence. This project aims to investigate nature and artificiality in the frame of the Japanese garden, how the experiences of beauty in nature differ from the beauty of artificially modified nature, how Japanese Zen rock garden exploits the inanimate objects and minimal aesthetic, and how the visionary who applied their own interpretation beyond the traditional method of garden making as creators. In this paper, historical analysis of Japanese garden's evolutions, the theoretical structure of phenomena of water wave formation and interference, mechanical analysis of wave generator, and computer simulation's scenographical visualization, all used together as methods for exploring to reimagine the new form of Japanese Zen garden.
